summary.objective: Minimize maximum native raster height; then minimize 8-neighbour planimetric path length, no corner cutting

input.crs_note: The embedded CRS identifier and axis declaration may differ; retain the WKT and use its actual X/Y projection with always_xy=True.
input.vertical_datum: NOT VERIFIED: no vertical CRS is encoded in the provided file
input.vertical_values: Native raster heights, metres; no geoid/vertical transform applied

straight_reference.note: NEW straight UTM line through user coordinates, NOT the unavailable historical 27 points

summary.boundary_warning: Both subcritical endpoint components touch the analysis boundary or NoData. A lower route outside the supplied/selected domain is not ruled out.
caveats: This is a topographic sublevel-connectivity test, not a hydraulic model or proof of a former river.
The threshold permits zero-depth contact; positive flow requires additional head and a finite cross-section.
Water direction, ice dams, erosion history, deposits, and time-varying topography are not reconstructed.
No sink filling, stream burning, smoothing, or manual lowering of roads/embankments is applied.
A centreline is not unique and its bends depend on raster topology and secondary cost.
10 m horizontal spacing and decimal raster values do not imply decimetre vertical accuracy.
No bathymetry is inferred from apparent lake surfaces in the terrain raster.
GeoJSON geometry is 2D; native, non-ellipsoidal elevations are stored as explicit properties.
Viewer terrain is display-only and uses native heights as local display heights; absolute globe altitude is not geodetically corrected.

terrain.raw_type: little-endian float32, row-major, north to south
terrain.pixel_registration: outer bounds; samples at pixel centres (subtract 0.5 on lookup)
terrain.vertical: native DEM heights, NOT converted to ellipsoidal height
